# Install, config and test-runner detection

- Install per-user (`~/.copilot/skills/lean-sdd-tdd`) when the target repo asserts its skill list (e.g. a test enumerating `.github/skills`); copying into `.github/skills` can break such tests. Run `node <skill>/scripts/sdd.mjs --root <repo> ...`.
- Build the target first (`npm run build`) if its CLI tests need build artifacts, before `gate`.
- `.sdd/config.json`: `scan:{include:[],exclude:["fixtures/**"]}` (globs; only comment-leading `@id` lines count; in Python, a line that starts a triple-quoted docstring or sits inside one also counts); `timeoutMs` globally or per check; check `changedCmd` with `{changedFiles}`/`{changedTests}` used by `gate --changed` (auto: `vitest related`, `jest --findRelatedTests`). `gate --changed` uses `changedTimeoutMs` (default 60s) so hub-file changes fail fast with `TIMEOUT`; narrow with `changedCmd` such as `["npx","vitest","run","{changedTests}","{changedScopes}"]` (scopes = package dirs). Always run the full `gate` (no `--changed`) before merge. Non-JS stacks get an auto `changedCmd` (no-pkg roots): Go `{changedGoPkgs}` (changed packages + reverse deps via `go list`), Rust `{changedCargoPkgs}` (`-p` changed crates + dependents via `cargo metadata`), Maven `{changedModulesCsv}` (changed modules + dependents + every upstream module they need, from the poms, so diamond dependencies resolve without `-am -amd`; falls back to the full run if the poms cannot be read), Go scoping also works in a repo without commits, Gradle `{changedGradleTasks}` (`:mod:cleanTest :mod:test` for changed modules plus dependents found from `project(':x')` references; not `buildDependents`, which misses later-evaluated dependents), CMake `{changedCtestRegex}` (`ctest -R` of changed test files). When a change cannot be scoped (go.mod/Cargo.*/root Gradle files, non-test C/C++ sources, CMake files, files outside any module) the full check runs and `! cmd …: cannot scope changes` is printed (for Rust: `cannot scope changes for the changed Cargo packages`). A `conftest.py` that defines only non-autouse fixtures the test never names (and no `pytest_*` hooks) is not an oracle of that test. `gate --changed` also scopes in tests whose recorded oracle files (e.g. a contract) changed. `impact` is file-granular (a note says so); the `tdd green` shared-implementation warning is per-`@implements`-block (ledger field `implBlocks`, #287; falls back to the whole file when the block cannot be delimited, and to file mtime for older ledger entries without the field). Hub detection (JS/TS relative-import graph): if > `hubThreshold` (0.25) of test files depend on the change, `hubFallbackCmd` runs (`{changedTests} {directTests}`); if that exceeds `hubMaxTests` (30) the check is skipped as INCOMPLETE instead of timing out. Workspace package names and tsconfig `paths` are followed. For hub changes the uncommitted diff is mapped to exported symbols (comment/whitespace-only ⇒ skipped; declarations mentioning the symbol are tainted transitively) so only tests that can reach them run; unknown diffs (non-exported/top-level code, `export *`) keep the whole hub set; an empty selection is INCOMPLETE, never an unscoped full run. Timeouts report `TIMEOUT`, not FAIL.
- `flaky: {retries?: 1, policy?: "fail"|"warn"}` (#303): a failed `test` check is re-run `retries` times (0 disables). A pass on re-run prints `cmd test FLAKY suspected …`: `fail` (default) keeps the gate FAIL, `warn` accepts it with the warning. Each flaky event is appended to `.sdd/tdd.jsonl` as `{type:"flaky",check,retry,policy,outcome}`. A consistent failure stays a plain failure. Write deterministic tests: no fixed `sleep`, injected clock/random, port 0, generous timeouts, isolate signal/kill tests.
- `prepare: {cmd, outputs?, inputs?, timeoutMs?}` in config (auto-set from the `build` script by `init`): `gate` runs it first and caches by input hash (`.sdd/prepare-cache.json`); skipped when inputs and `outputs` are unchanged.

## Test runners per stack
- Go/Rust: default `testCmd` is `go test ./... -run '{IDU}(_|$)'` (e.g. `TEST_CALC_001`, name test funcs `TestTEST_CALC_001_…`) / `cargo test {idu}` (`test_calc_001_…`). Placeholders: `{id}`, `{idu}` (complete annotated function/method when resolvable), `{IDU}` (UPPER_SNAKE). Direct Cargo commands resolve the full module-qualified name and add `-- --exact`. Go and Rust were verified end-to-end (Red/Green/gate). Rust inline `#[cfg(test)]` tests protect their test regions and shared test helpers/data, excluding annotated production code. Go `[build failed]` is a load error, not a Red.
- Maven / Gradle (`./gradlew` if present) / CMake+CTest are auto-detected (verified: Maven 3.9 + JUnit5, Gradle 8.14 + JUnit5, CMake/ctest). Name the test method / ctest test so it contains the lowercase ID (`test_calc_001_add` for `TEST-CALC-001`); `{idu}` is substituted into `-Dtest=*#*{idu}*`, `--tests *{idu}*` and `ctest -R`. Gradle runs through a temporary init script (`failOnNoMatchingTests=false` + a `Tests run: N` total per task), so multi-project builds work from the root and a subproject without a match does not fail the build; multi-module Maven works from the root too (zero-test modules are ignored when another module ran tests). Maven `gate --changed` runs `-pl <changed modules> -amd` (dependents included; falls back to the full check when changes are outside any module); Gradle `--changed` runs the full check. POM/Gradle build-script errors are load errors, not Red. Gradle 8 needs JDK ≤ 24 (set `JAVA_HOME`). CMake builds into `build/` (git-ignore it); it configures once, builds incrementally with the log shown only on failure, and `--changed` runs the full (incremental) check.
- Makefile (`make test TEST={idu}` — your `test` target must pass `$(TEST)` to the runner to filter; verified with a C runner) and .NET (`*.sln`/`*.slnx`/`*.csproj` → `dotnet test --filter FullyQualifiedName~{idu}`; verified with xUnit: `tdd red/green/refactor`, `gate`, `gate --changed`) are auto-detected after the language-specific stacks. In a nested layout only csproj files referencing `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` (or `<IsTestProject>true`) become `projects`; test-less class libraries do not. xUnit, NUnit and MSTest all work through the VSTest filter (`FullyQualifiedName~{idu}`); `{idu}` is the lowercase ID when the file contains it, else the method name below `@id` (`[Fact]`/`[Test]`/`[TestCase(..)]`/`[TestMethod]`/`[DataRow(..)]` lines are skipped; `[TestCase]`/`[DataRow]` rows run as one test). `bin/` and `obj/` next to a project file are never scanned for `@id`, even without `.gitignore`. Within one sdd process (a batch `tdd red A B C`, or several checks on the same target) a repeat `dotnet test` gets `--no-build` only when the previous run built cleanly (no `error CS/MSB/NETSDK/NU`) and no tracked file (other than `.sdd/`) changed since; a changed tree, a failed build or a different target always rebuilds, and single runs always build. The default .NET check has `changedCmd` `sh -c 'for p in "$@"; do dotnet test "$p" --nologo || r=1; done; exit $r' sdd {changedTestProjects}`: `{changedTestProjects}` = changed test projects plus test projects that (transitively) `ProjectReference` a changed project (csproj / `Directory.Build.props` references, owner = nearest csproj of a changed file). A changed `.sln`/`.slnx`/`Directory.Build.*`/`Directory.Packages.props`/`global.json`/`nuget.config`, or no changed file inside a project, prints `cannot scope changes for {changedTestProjects} — running the full check`. In a nested layout the test project's `dependsOn` is derived from its `ProjectReference`s (and shared props above it). `tdd stub` supports C# (see references/stubs.md); the default `changedTimeoutMs` is 60 s, raise it for slow builds. Weak-Red detection attributes a name-less `NotImplementedException` via the first stack frame.
- Test-name fallback: if the test file does not contain the lowercase ID, `{idu}` becomes the name of the test declared right below `@id` (skipping annotations/comments), so camelCase JUnit methods (`void addsNumbers()`) work without renaming. Keep the `@id` comment directly above the test.
- PHP (`composer.json`/`phpunit.xml` → `phpunit --do-not-cache-result --filter {idu} {file}`, `vendor/bin/phpunit` if present; PHPUnit 13.4+ uses `--do-not-record-test-run-history` instead, detected with `--version` for both TDD and checks), Julia (`Project.toml` → `julia --project=. {file}`, whole file per run); the default `gate` check is `Pkg.test()`, which needs a package registry even for stdlib test deps — when it fails with a registry/network error and `test/runtests.jl` exists the check prints `INFRA: ...` and falls back to `julia --project=. test/runtests.jl` and R (`DESCRIPTION` → `testthat::test_file`, whole file per run; verified with testthat 3; set `R_LIBS_USER` if testthat is in a user library) are auto-detected. Name PHP test methods so they contain the lowercase ID. Existing configs are not rewritten: override both PHPUnit commands when upgrading.
- Other stacks (C/C++/Java/…, verified with plain `sh run_tests.sh <name-filter>` runners): `init` warns that testCmd is a Node fallback; set `testCmd` yourself to a runner that takes the test-name filter, e.g. `["sh","run_tests.sh","{idu}"]` (the runner must exit non-zero when no test matches), and a `checks` entry for the full suite. Annotate with `//` or `/* */` comments; `.c .h .cc .cpp .cxx .hpp .hh .java` are scanned.
- `init` re-run keeps an existing config (delete it to re-detect).

## Monorepos
- Go module boundaries are independent: `init` registers every nested `go.mod`, even with a root Go module or another enclosing nested module, and retains the root checks. `go test ./...` does not check nested modules (#161). Delete an existing config and re-run `init` to opt into this detection.
- For direct Go `testCmd`, `tdd` adds verbose reporting and replaces `-run` with the exact annotated function or literal `t.Run` hierarchy (regex metacharacters escaped). `-json` is supported for target verdicts and diagnostics. A parent/package failure alone is not the subtest's Red (#161–#162).
- With a nested `--root`, `gate --changed` converts Git paths to that root, ignores changes outside it, and checks affected evidence/projects; quoted paths and renames are supported. `gate --changed --baseline <ref>` also scopes everything committed since `<ref>`; a changed non-code `artifacts` file puts its consumers' REQs in scope (#254).
- Polyglot monorepo: when the repo root has no manifest, `init` finds nested manifests (go.mod, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, pom.xml, …) and writes `projects: [{root, testCmd, checks}]`. `tdd` runs a test with its project's `testCmd` in that directory (`{file}` is relative to it); `gate` runs every project's checks as `<root>:<name>` in its cwd; `gate --changed` skips projects with no changed files.
- Mixed monorepo: if the root has a manifest (e.g. package.json), nested projects of a *different* stack (services/go) are still added to `projects`; nested projects of the same stack (npm workspaces) stay with the root. `projects[].dependsOn: ["libs/shared"]` (manual) makes `gate --changed` run the project when a dependency root changes; the path may be any shared directory (e.g. `contract/` shared by a TS API and a Python worker), and `gate --changed` hints when root-owned files changed that no project depends on. Root checks (no `cwd`) are skipped when every changed file is inside a nested project. A project check with `changedCmd`/`hubFallbackCmd` gets `{changedFiles}`/`{changedTests}`/`{changedScopes}` relative to the project root; a dependency-only change runs the full project check. `dependsOn` is transitive (a project that depends on another project's root also inherits that project's `dependsOn`, #241). `projects[].dependsOnMode: "referenced"` (#287) makes `impact` on a shared data file reach that project only when one of its files names the file's path or basename; the default (`declared`) keeps the over-approximation and lists such projects on a `declared dependsOn only` line. `artifacts: {"contract/x.json": ["src/a.ts"]}` declares files depending on a non-code artifact so `impact` traverses it (#242); in `gate --changed` a changed artifact also runs the project holding one of its consumers (#308).
- Filters are token-anchored (#141): default node/vitest/jest patterns are `{id}(?![0-9A-Za-z])` (TEST-S-001 does not select TEST-S-0011); Maven/Gradle use a suffix match (`*#*{idu}`, `*{idu}`). `{idu}` keeps the case the name has in the test file (NUnit/xUnit `FullyQualifiedName~` is case-sensitive).
- Runtime exact selection (#164) refines the stored placeholder commands: CTest uses an anchored full function-name regex; PHPUnit uses `/::<method>(?:\s+with data set .*)?$/`; .NET uses `FullyQualifiedName=<namespace>.<class>.<method>` when the qualified declaration is resolvable, plus normal-verbosity console results. Parsed outcomes belong to the exact target, not a longer sibling.
- Git is optional (#163): nested manifest/project discovery, import graphs and C# stubs fall back to filesystem discovery. `gate --changed` cannot infer an empty diff from unavailable Git; it reports the unavailable scope and runs a full gate.
- Gradle generated init scripts live under the project's `.sdd/`, are removed after the command, and report `Tests run`, `Failures` and `Skipped` for TDD, full checks and scoped checks (#165). Disabled/skipped-only Gradle/CTest/Julia full checks are INCOMPLETE, not PASS; mixed executed/skipped runs remain valid.
- Exact ownership refinements (#171–#180): Cargo also selects the owning package and executable (including out-of-line unit modules); Maven/Gradle selectors use the fully qualified class/method. Gradle emits per-test identities and Java XML reports are refreshed before TDD attribution. Default CTest selection discovers a unique method/ID registration rather than assuming the C function name is the registration. PHPUnit dataset patterns span newlines. .NET custom `TestName`/`DisplayName` cases retain method identity; skipped-only normal/minimal VSTest checks are INCOMPLETE. Direct `julia --project=. {file}` runners enable verbose nested summaries without source edits; custom Julia runners must provide observable target summaries.
- Batch-3 refinements (#181–#188): local Rust test modules/data and C/C++ oracle includes participate in evidence hashes transitively (annotated production is excluded; other local includes are conservatively protected). Rust wildcard imports retain conservative cross-crate impact. Nested Java selectors use `$`; nested C# classes/records use `+`, and direct .NET TDD scopes to the owning csproj. Maven/Gradle must expose fresh target results; overloaded JUnit method names are refused, so give each test a unique name within its class. Inline JUnit annotations and PHPUnit lifecycle attributes/aliases participate in isolated hashes. CTest registration ID delimiters may be punctuation or underscores; names are selected uniquely, escaped and anchored, and standard assertions in reachable C helpers count as Red without treating unrelated signals as evidence.
- Julia custom runners: `["julia","--compile=min","--project=.","test/runner.jl","{file}"]` preserves the launcher's `ARGS[1]`; automatic `-e` verbosity injection applies only when `{file}` is the actual executed script operand. Custom `AbstractTestSet` types are not given new constructor keywords and must print target summaries. Complete hyphenated IDs are matched exactly; `--expect` searches only target failure blocks. Explained `--retest` accepts an executed passing changed target as weak Red even when a sibling fails.
- Wave-2a (#189–#198): local support/oracle closure now includes Rust raw/concat manifest paths, nested path modules, bare angle headers, local Java/PHP/C# inherited support and Julia includes. Composed/qualified/aliased/multiline lifecycle declarations respect class ownership. Default PHPUnit filters are class-qualified; direct .NET TDD adds a fresh TRX logger under `.sdd/results/` and aggregates every row selected by the exact method filter. Generic fixtures use bounded selection plus mandatory runtime method metadata rather than an impossible nongeneric equality. CTest whitespace names and C++ pretty-function assertions retain attribution. Qualified standard Julia macro/type spellings get nested-summary verbosity too.
- Wave-2b (#199–#205): Cargo `include!` tests retain enclosing modules and require explicit `--lib`/`--bin NAME`/`--test NAME`/`--example NAME` when shared across targets. C/C++ oracle discovery uses the owning compilation database's include paths, defines and forced includes; unresolved macro inputs are refused. Julia standard `Test` aliases get nested verbosity; generic NUnit TRX method names accept argument rows but not longer siblings. Generated production ownership and handwritten annotation timing are detailed in `stubs.md`.
- **Elixir / ExUnit** (`mix.exs` → `mix test {file}`, check `mix test`): TDD rewrites `{file}` to `file:LINE` of the `test "..."` following the `# @id`, so only that test runs and a failing sibling is never attributed to it. Tests are discovered as `test "..."` / `describe "..."` (reported as `test <describe> <name>`) with optional `@tag`; `@id`/`@verifies` live in `#` comments above the test. `N tests, 0 failures` with every test excluded/skipped (`@tag :skip`, `--only` filters) is not Green or Red; `** (CompileError)` and `module X is not available` are load errors.
- `generated: ["contract/**"]` (#293): paths/globs of build outputs a test reads; they are dropped from the oracle dependency set (no "oracle dependency changed" refusal, but also no oracle checking of them). `[src: file:line]` provenance in a REQ row is excluded from the row hash, so re-anchoring lines does not invalidate Green. Not yet handled: crate-wide Rust oracle narrowing, conftest.py per-test consistency, drift checks of `[src:]` lines in the gate.
- Wave-15 r21b (#308/#301 decisions): a changed `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` whose workspace `members` live under a project dir runs that project's checks and is not reported as "root-owned data". Not changed (no repro or needs redesign): `--baseline` after a merge (plain `git diff <ref>` already covers merges), scoped-Rust rerun de-duplication, runtime-read contract consumers (declare them via `dependsOn`/`artifacts`), project-granular impact noise.

- `specEditPolicy: "reapprove"` (default unset = warn only): on a T1 feature (no approval lock), `tdd refactor` after the wording of an already-Green REQ row changed is refused unless `--wording "<why the behaviour is unchanged>"` is given (that flag is the re-approval; a behaviour change needs `tdd red` then `tdd green`). Until then `gate` keeps failing with `changed in the spec`. Ledgers and configs without the key behave as before.
- `artifactStaleness: true` (#309, opt-in): Green/Refactor entries record `artifactShas` for each config `artifacts` file whose path or basename the test file names; editing such a file stales that test (`artifact <path> changed since last Green/Refactor` → `tdd refactor <id>` or `tdd red <id> --retest "<reason>"` + `tdd green`). Entries without `artifactShas` keep the old behaviour.
- `artifactGranularity: "test"` (#312, opt-in, with `artifactStaleness`): a test's artifact hashes consider only its own `@id` lines plus the preamble before the first `@id`, so sibling tests that never name the artifact stay valid (re-record with `tdd refactor` to apply). `tdd refactor --stale` also selects artifact-stale tests. `impact <artifact>` lists only files that name a declared artifact; `impact <Cargo.toml>` reaches the workspace members' REQs (`members` globs like `crates/*` are expanded, also for `gate --changed` project attribution).
- `preambleGranularity: "symbol"` (#300, opt-in): by default a test's evidence covers its own `@id` region plus the whole shared preamble, so editing any helper/fixture stales every test in the file. With `"symbol"` the preamble is split into (a) imports/`use`/includes and other non-definition statements (any change still stales all tests) and (b) top-level helper/fixture definitions (`function`/`class`/`const`/`let`/`type`, Python `def`/`class`/`NAME =`, Rust `fn`/`const`/`static`/`struct`/`enum`/`trait`/`impl`): a change stales only tests whose own body (transitively through other helpers) names that helper. Supported: TS/JS, Python, Rust (Rust `fn` helpers were already scoped); other languages keep the whole-preamble behaviour. Ledgers recorded before enabling still match their old hash while unchanged.
- Scope confidence (r24a, design 3.1): `gate --changed` records each run check as `exact` (scoped, or a project whose files changed) or `widened` (full run because the change could not be scoped) and prints `scope: exact=N widened=N unknown=N` (`--json` adds a `scope` object). `unknown` = changed files no project root, `dependsOn`, `artifacts`, or root check claims. `scopePolicy: "warn"` (default when the key is absent) warns with the file list; `"strict"` fails (`init` writes `strict` into NEW configs only). `unscoped: ["misc/**"]` and `--allow-unscoped <glob[,glob]>` waive files (the flag is recorded as a `scope-waiver` ledger entry). Always ignored: `**/*.md`, `.github/**`, `LICENSE`, `.sdd/**`. A root `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`/`rust-toolchain*`/`.cargo/config*`, JS `package.json`/lockfiles, Python `pyproject.toml`/`requirements*.txt`/lockfiles run the checks of every project of that ecosystem (a project is of an ecosystem when its root holds the manifest). The "no changed files … skipped" messages state the input closure they were computed from.
